settings.mention_hint: the agent answers when someone @mentions it in a comment

settings.skills_mode_native: Native — files the engine opens on demand

settings.model_credentials_hint_html: what this agent runs with; takes effect on the next run. Keys and profiles live in Settings → AI engines
settings.skills_delivery_hint_html: how granted skills reach the model. Auto follows the engine: engines that discover skills get them as files and open what they need; the rest get every skill pasted into the prompt (~12k tokens up front). Skills set to "Always in the prompt" on /skills/ stay in the prompt either way.
settings.repo_requirement_hint: tasks moving into a stage assigned to this agent get blocked if no repo is linked
settings.works_without_repo_hint: (research, text polish, ideation — anything that doesn't touch code)
settings.valid_stages_hint: tick the stages this agent runs on, plus its max turns per stage
settings.valid_stages_hint_no_turns: tick the stages this agent runs on; {engine} has no turn limit, so there is none to set

settings.auditor_hint: tick the stages where the auditor reviews the run when it ends; the settings are optional (left empty, it uses the auditor's own)
settings.modes_hint: not columns: the agent runs when someone calls it. Prompts, skills and MCP are picked per mode just as per column.

skills.title: Skills per stage
skills.intro_html: Workspace skills this agent gets on each stage; they are written in Skills. With an engine that discovers skills (Claude Code) the model sees each skill's name and description and opens the one it needs; with other engines, and for skills set to "Always in the prompt", the whole text goes into the prompt. "Skills delivery", in Settings, can force one way or the other.
skills.pick_stage: Pick at least one valid stage in the Settings tab.
skills.system_intro: Thulu adds these on its own: some to every run, others when the stage has their MCP server. Untick one to leave it out of this agent's runs on this stage.
skills.system_run_off_warning: octopus-run is off: runs on this stage will not learn where the repos and the output dir are, who commits and opens the PR, or what to leave when they finish. Without it an agent can move its own task or lose its report. Turn it off only if this agent's prompt already covers that.

mcp.title: MCP servers per stage
mcp.intro_html: Which MCP servers the agent can use on each stage. Ticking a server grants what its scope covers; tools granted by name are picked under Tools. Servers are registered in MCPs.
mcp.no_tools_html: No MCP servers yet. Register them in MCPs.
mcp.tools_title: Choose which tools of {server} this stage may call
mcp.tools_unknown_title: The daemon could not read this server's tool list — it may be stopped, or it isn't reachable. The whole server is granted.
mcp.default_unknown_title: Granted by bare name. This server has no descriptor saying which tools it grants without a scope, so no tool is shown as ticked and the server applies its own default. Pick tools, or untick and tick the server to grant every tool explicitly.
mcp.drawer_untick_hint: Unticking every tool removes the server from this stage.

grant_bare.admin: Ticked grants read, write and admin.
grant_bare.all: Ticked grants all of its tools.
grant_bare.unknown: With no descriptor there is no telling what the server grants with no tools picked.

grant_by_name.one: {count} tool is granted by name only.
grant_by_name.other: {count} tools are granted by name only.

mcp.drawer_all_scoped: All, except the ones granted by name

group_hint.deploy: They merge PRs, dispatch workflows and approve deployments. No scope includes them: tick them only on the stage that has to do that.
group_hint.board: They read and change tasks on the workspace's other boards. No scope includes them: tick them only if this stage works across boards.
group_hint.other: No scope includes them: the server grants them only when named one by one.

mcp.deploy_template_title: Grants thulu-github@read plus run_dispatch, run_watch and run_logs: what a stage that deploys through GitHub Actions needs

grant_stage.read: On this stage it grants read.
grant_stage.write: On this stage it grants read and write.
grant_stage.admin: On this stage it grants read, write and admin.
grant_stage.other: On this stage it grants the {scope} scope.

list.one: On this stage it grants {count} tool picked by hand.
list.other: On this stage it grants {count} tools picked by hand.

mcp.deploy_note: run_dispatch starts GitHub Actions workflows: the GitHub App needs the Actions: write permission.

prompts.intro: Per-stage files are named after the stage id, so a prompt written for a custom stage lives or dies with it. Every save is kept: open a file and use History to read or restore an earlier version.
prompts.status_missing: Missing: write it and every stage without its own prompt uses it
prompts.orphans_hint: Files for a stage this agent no longer runs on, or one that left every board. No run loads them: delete them, or move their text to one of the stages above.
prompts.other_intro_html: Other .md files in the agent directory not covered by the conventions above.

confirm.prune_message: Removes this agent's config for {stages} — the labels and the matching prompts/*.md and auditor/*.md files. Unsaved edits in this pane are discarded.
confirm.discard_prompt_edits: Edits to this prompt will be lost.
confirm.delete_file_message: This removes the file from the agent.
confirm.discard_prompt_message: Your edits to this prompt will be lost.
confirm.discard_settings_message: Your changes to this agent will be lost.
confirm.delete_agent_message: It leaves the list and the pickers, and its prompts stay in the history. Tasks that had it assigned keep naming it: if you later create another agent with this name, those tasks run with the new one.

delete_agent_used.one: {count} task or project template names it today.
delete_agent_used.other: {count} tasks or project templates name it today.

role.viewer: Your role is read-only: you see the agent's settings but cannot change them.

optimizer.title: Large reads
optimizer.hint_html: Hands large file reads to a cheaper model so the agent spends fewer tokens; Suggest leaves it to the agent, Enforce always does it. That model runs with the workspace's default credential for its engine, set in Settings → AI engines.
optimizer.engines_missing_html: An engine without a usable default credential can't be picked. Set one in Settings → AI engines.
optimizer.engine_required: Pick the engine of the model that reads large files.
optimizer.model_required: Name the model that reads large files.
